title: Flat scalar extension for sections on an algebraic stack
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $R$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, let $p:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism from an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put $\mathcal X_S=\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}S$ with projection $q$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For a sheaf $\mathcal A$ on the big fppf site of $\mathcal X$, write $\mathcal A_S$ for precomposition with $q$, using the restriction convention of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. If $\mathcal A$ is a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebra, then $\mathcal A_S$ is quasi-coherent, and restriction takes any surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of such algebras to a surjection $\mathcal A_S\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B_S$. The canonical map of $S$-algebras $$\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\otimes_R S\longrightarrow\Gamma(\mathcal X_S,\mathcal A_S),\qquad a\otimes s\longmapsto q^*a\cdot p_S^*s,$$ is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal A$; here $p_S:\mathcal X_S\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is the second projection, and tensor extension uses [def-weil-module-base-change]. For $\mathcal A=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ the comparison sends $1\otimes s$ to the structural section $p_S^*s$. There are no finite-generation or Noetherian hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0765 (lemma-flat-comparison), degree zero, and Tag 0771 (proposition-loc-qcoh-flat-base-change), (4), applied over affine schemes to a quasi-coherent algebra. Quasi-coherent objects have the comparison property by stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent). Pullback preservation and flat exactness: stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WH (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent) and stacks-cohomology.tex Tag 076X (lemma-flat-pullback-quasi-coherent). On the big site these tensor pullbacks agree with the precomposition restriction by the cartesian comparison in 06WK; multiplication and the structural unit are preserved by their displayed pure-tensor formulas.

proof.text: Apply scheme-test restriction to the underlying module of $\mathcal A$. It gives quasi-coherent scheme modules $A_x$ and canonical isomorphisms $u^*A_y\simeq A_x$ for every arrow $x\to y$ over $u$. Precomposition along $q$ is therefore quasi-coherent and retains the algebra operations. If $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$, the scheme-test maps $A_x\to B_x$ are surjective. On a test $z$ of $\mathcal X_S$ the restricted map is precisely $A_{qz}\to B_{qz}$; the converse surjection criterion proves it is a sheaf surjection. This proves both restriction assertions, without a flatness assumption on $q$.

source.place: Tags 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), 06WH (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent), and 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent); scheme-test surjection and restriction formulation.

proof.text: The same scheme-test isomorphisms show that $\mathcal A$ is locally quasi-coherent and has flat comparison maps in the terminology of the higher-image theorem. Apply that theorem to the given qcqs morphism $p$, in degree zero. The resulting module sheaf $G=p_*\mathcal A$ on the big site of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally quasi-coherent and has invertible comparison along $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, since $R\to S$ is flat. Its scheme restrictions $G_R,G_S$ satisfy $c:g^*G_R\xrightarrow{\sim}G_S$. By the displayed degree-zero direct-image formula, their sections on the whole schemes are $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and $\Gamma(\mathcal X_S,\mathcal A_S)$; the section restriction is $q^*$.

Apply the affine pullback-sections isomorphism to the quasi-coherent scheme module $G_R$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, taking both affine opens to be the whole schemes. Compose it with the section map of $c$. This gives an isomorphism $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\otimes_RS\simeq\Gamma(\mathcal X_S,\mathcal A_S)$ sending $a\otimes s$ to $s\cdot q^*a$. The scalar action is the structural action, so this is exactly $q^*a\,p_S^*s$. Both the affine comparison and $c$ are defined by section restriction and scalar multiplication.

Write this map as $\theta$. For pure tensors, $\theta((a\otimes s)(b\otimes t))=q^*(ab)p_S^*(st)=(q^*a\,p_S^*s)(q^*b\,p_S^*t)$, and $\theta(1\otimes1)=1$. Additivity extends this identity to sums of pure tensors; also $\theta(1\otimes s)=p_S^*s$. For an algebra map $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, restriction commutes with $h$, so $h_S(\theta(a\otimes s))=q^*h(a)p_S^*s=\theta(h(a)\otimes s)$. These formulas give the $S$-algebra structure and naturality; the bijective module comparison in step 3 is consequently an algebra isomorphism. Taking $\mathcal A=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ gives the required structural-section normalization.
